Customer Behavior Analysis Dashboard

ExcelPythonPandasNumPySQL ServerPower BI3,900 records

An end-to-end customer behavior analytics project that transforms raw customer shopping data into business insights using Python, SQL Server, and Power BI.

Raw Dataset→Python ETL→Data Cleaning→EDA→SQL Server→Business Analytics→Power BI Dashboard→Business Insights
Python ETL
  • Loaded customer shopping data using Pandas.
  • Handled missing review ratings.
  • Standardized column names.
  • Created age groups.
  • Converted purchase frequency into numeric values.
  • Prepared the cleaned dataset for SQL Server.
Exploratory analysis covered
Purchasing trendsProduct categoriesSeasonsCustomer segmentsSubscription behaviorCustomer loyalty
SQL business questions (10 queries in SQL Server)
  • Revenue by gender and by age group
  • Subscriber vs non-subscriber spending
  • Discount impact
  • Shipping type analysis
  • Top-rated products and top products within categories
SQL techniques
AggregationsGROUP BYCASECTEsSubqueriesWindow FunctionsROW_NUMBER
Findings from the project analysis
Clothing contributed approximately 45% of revenue.
$104K clothing revenue from approximately $233K total revenue.
Average spending was approximately $59.49 for subscribers and $59.87 for non-subscribers.
Approximately 80% of customers were classified as loyal based on 10+ previous purchases.
Power BI dashboard preview

Dashboard KPIs: 3.9K customers · 3.75 average review rating · $59.76 average purchase · 27% subscribers. Filters for subscription status, gender, category, and shipping type.

View GitHubDashboard Preview

ProblemUnderstand customer purchasing behavior, segments, subscription behavior, and loyalty.

Data / Input3,900 customer shopping records.

TechnologyExcel, Python, Pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, Power BI.

ProcessPython ETL and cleaning: missing ratings, standardized columns, age groups, numeric purchase frequency.

AnalysisEDA plus 10 SQL Server queries using CTEs, subqueries, window functions, and CASE segmentation.

ResultClothing led revenue at about 45%; subscribers did not spend more than non-subscribers ($59.49 vs $59.87); about 80% of customers were loyal.

Business / Practical ValueShows which categories and customer groups drive revenue, giving insights for retention strategy.
